title: Triangle decompositions of typical graphs of fixed density (Keevash, Counting designs, Theorem 2.1, weaker form)
abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of a weaker, fixed-density form of Theorem 2.1 of P. Keevash, Counting designs (J. Eur. Math. Soc. 20, 2018). density G is |E(G)| / C(n, 2); IsTypical G c h says that every nonempty set S of at most h vertices has (1 ± |S| c) d(G)^|S| n common neighbours; Tridivisible G says that every degree is even and 3 divides |E(G)|; IsTriangleDecomposition G D says that D is a family of triangles of G and every edge lies in exactly one of them. typical_triangle_decomposition: there is h such that for every d0 > 0 there are c0 > 0 and n0 such that every (c0, h)-typical tridivisible graph on n ≥ n0 vertices with density at least d0 has a triangle decomposition. This is weaker than the article in two ways: the density is bounded below by a fixed constant (the article allows d(G) > n^(-10^-7) with c < c0 d(G)^(10^6)), and the typicality is (c, h)-typicality for an absolute, not explicit, h (the article assumes c-typicality, which concerns only degrees and pairs). One statement.
